newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Russia reassures Kuwait on position with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Russia reassures Kuwait on position with Iraq.

text.p: A senior Russian diplomat has reassured Kuwait about Russia's compliance with U.N.-imposed sanctions against Iraq following Kuwaiti concern over a recent Moscow-Baghdad oil deal.

Visiting head of the Middle East department at the Russian foreign ministry, Andrey Vdovin told the official Kuwait News Agency late on Wednesday: "The actual implementation of the oil deal...will not start until the sanctions are lifted."
"Russia will not take any action that would violate the international legitimacy and harm the State of Kuwait."
The United Nations imposed strict economic sanctions against Baghdad after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov has said the $3.5 billion deal signed on Friday would be implemented regardless of the United Nations sanctions imposed on Iraq since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

But Zarubezhneft deputy chairman Yuri Agababov, whose firm has a stake in the deal, said on Monday: "The U.N. sanctions will be fully observed. We are not looking to violate any sanctions. The only things that will go forward now are things that do not violate the sanctions."
Vdovin carried a message from Russian foreign minister Yevgeny Primakov to his counterpart Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah.

"Primakov affirmed in his message...the Russian Federation's position represented by calling Iraq to comply with all U.N. resolutions related to its aggression against the State of Kuwait including those related to economic sanctions," it said.
The 23-year deal is for the development of seven to eight billion barrels of reserves in southern Iraq's west Qurnah oilfield.
